To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a free, easy-to-use web application that allows users to perform classification using logistic regression with variable selection and compare its performance to other classification methods.

(1) logistic regression can be an effective and interpretable tool for gene expression-based cancer classification, and (2) we have developed a web-based program that implements logistic regression that can be used to compare classification methods.

logistic regression can be used as an alternative method to more sophisticated algorithms for disease classification and that a web application can be developed with a minimal amount programming and free software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of methods to identify genes that are associated with disease.
the development of a new tool that allows the classification of gene expression data using logistic regression.
the development of a new web-based tool for gene expression data classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the web application developed in this project is a good example of how bioinformatics laboratories can use free, open-source software to develop a web-based tool for analysis of high-throughput gene data.
the logistic regression model can be used as an alternative for the more sophisticated classification methods.
logistic regression can be used as an initial screening tool for the identification of important genes and pathways in disease classification, and it can be implemented easily in a web application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a simple and effective classification method for high-throughput gene-expression data and we have made the method and its results available to our collaborators through an easy-to-use web application.
we developed an efficient and user-friendly web application to facilitate the classification of gene expression profiles using logistic regression.

we have built a tool for classification of gene expression data using logistic regression with variable selection, implemented the tool as a web-based application and made the application freely available for use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
simple statistical tools, such as logistic regression, are often overlooked in the analysis of high-throughput data and can be used as an effective first step in classification analysis.
logistic regression can be used as an alternative method for classification of high-throughput gene-expression data.
simple methods can be very effective and should be used in conjunction with more sophisticated methods for the classification of gene expression data.
